# kayjs-cms

> A CMS for kay sites: content edited on the page it renders, and collection screens.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- The app writes no marker: in edit mode kay marks each element rendering an entry's field itself, `data-kay-field="<collection>:<slug>[@<locale>]:<path>"`, each segment URI-encoded, the path dotted with list indexes (`sections.1.heading`). A field in an attribute is `data-kay-field-<attribute>`, a field sharing its element's text sits between `<!--kay-field …-->` and `<!--/kay-field-->`, fields are marked wherever the data is read, a component handed the entry's data included, and a Markdown body is `data-kay-body="<collection>:<slug>"` or a `kay-body` comment pair.
- The body's path is the `BODY` symbol, never a string, so a data field named `body` stays a data field.
- Outside edit mode the page is unchanged and the editor is not rendered.
- Above an entry's form the editor names the fields of it the page cannot let a click reach (`EditorProps.unclickable`): a transformed value, an island's props, a frozen object.
- The editor panel never covers what it edits: from 64rem it docks to the right and pads the page's `body` by its width, below that (and always below 40rem) it is a bottom sheet padding the `body` by its height, so the page keeps its width and a fixed header at the top stays in view (at the side the panel starts under a header fixed or sticky across the top, at most 240px tall and touching it, found by itself; one added later is found on the next scroll or resize). A visitor drags or arrow-keys its inner edge (a focusable `separator`) to resize it, switches the dock with the head's button (from 40rem), and hides it to a button; the dock, sizes and hidden state are kept in `localStorage` (`kcms-editor`). The dev tool docked at the right or bottom publishes `--kay-dev-inset-right` and `-bottom` on `html`, and the panel sits beside it, clamped so the page keeps 22rem (10rem tall); the open panel publishes what it holds as `--kay-panel-right` or `-bottom` on `html`, which the dev tool's bar and floating drawer keep out of (the collapsed button publishes itself the same way; the bar publishes its measured room at a bottom corner as `--kay-dev-bar-bottom-left` or `-right`). A click on a marked element scrolls it above the bottom sheet, and an entry's sticky header stays on one line. `html.kcms-editing` carries `--kcms-width` and `--kcms-height` for a site that wants to line up with the panel.
- Unsaved edits of the on-page editor are kept in `localStorage` (`kcms:draft:<entry>`, `browserKeeper()`, a week at most), cleared on save, Reset and Stop editing, and brought back after a reload, a crash or in a second tab with a note; a draft made from an older version of the entry (or, for an entry with no version, from another saved copy) is dropped with a note, never offered, and the write waits for the pause before the page renders again. A reload or a link with edits unsaved on the entries the page shows asks first (`guardLeave`), and Stop editing asks too: Keep editing or Drop them and stop. A conflict lists the fields both sides changed and offers Keep my edits or Take their version (`drafts.adopt`).
- Draft rendering happens on the server: the editor sends the changed entries, kay renders the page with them and swaps it in, islands kept. An entry the schema refuses shows its saved text while the others keep their preview, and the editor names it; a status line (`role="status"`) says `Updating the page…` while it renders, the drafts render again after in-app navigation, and for five minutes after a forge save (kept in `localStorage`) it says the live site may still show the old content, also after leaving edit mode and coming back.
- Every change goes through one API, `POST` and `DELETE /api/cms/entries/:collection/:slug` (and `GET`, which answers `{ collection, entry }` as the editor opens the entry, `?locale=` for a localized one, a 404 for a missing entry), `POST …/:slug/publish`, `POST …/:slug/duplicate` (a draft copy, answering its `slug`), `GET /api/cms/entries/:collection` (the entries a reference can pick, `[{ slug, title }]`) `POST …/:slug/move?direction=up|down` and `POST /api/cms/markdown` (`{ markdown }`, answering the sanitized `{ html }` of the editor's Preview, 422 for a text kay cannot read), from the sidebar and from the screens alike. kay validates the data against the schema and names the file; kay writes nothing, the configured `files` saver does.
- An `imageField()` or `fileField()` holds a path the site serves, or an http(s) address: any other scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`) fails the schema, whatever the editor typed. The rest, uploads, the picker, limits, alt text and sizes, is in [Uploads and image fields](llms/uploads.md).
- The app imports kayjs-ui's theme. The screens and the editor render their own `Toaster` and `TooltipHost`, which render nothing while the app's are mounted; kayjs-ui is a peer dependency, so both resolve the one copy that guard lives in.
- Every text the screens and the editor show is looked up in the app's catalogs under a `cms.<area>.<name>` key before its English, `cms.editor.title` for `Edit this page`, through `wording` from `kay/words`, so a site words it once in `src/messages/<locale>.ts`; the editor's forms read the page's locale in the browser. kayjs-cms ships the French of every key, read on a French page with no setup and overridden key by key in the app's own catalog; another language is a `cms` block in `src/messages/<locale>.ts`. Every key is listed in [Texts and languages](llms/words.md).
- The screens are closed without a `guard`: kayjs-cms has no users of its own, so a guard is kayjs-auth's, or `passwordGuard(password)` for a small site (a sign-in screen at `<prefix>/sign-in`). A visitor refused with a 401 is sent to sign in and back to the exact page; the header names who is signed in and signs out; `cms({ roles })` limits a role to `publish`, `delete`, `upload` and `redirects` (the screens disable what it may not do; `cms({ member })` gives a custom guard its roles); an editor whose sign-in ended mid-edit is told so and keeps the edits: [Options](llms/options.md#signing-in-and-roles).
- Edit mode is kay's preview mode, so the app sets `preview.secret`. An edit cookie or link reads through the API only the entries the pages it rendered in edit mode read (the editor's own entries; a signed-in editor the guard admits reads any), and leaves edit mode. It saves, publishes, deletes and uploads only under `kay dev` without a `guard`: with a `guard` every write needs it, and any other server without one (`NODE_ENV` unset included) refuses every write from an edit cookie or link and warns at boot, naming `cms({ guard })`, since the cookie is tied to no user. The scope is kept in memory per server, so after a restart, or on another replica, the page is loaded again before its editor reads; `editedEntry(request, collection, slug)` from `kay/server` is what the API reads it from.

## Setup

`kay add cms` installs the packages and adds `cms()` to `extensions`.

```ts
import { cms, forgejo } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-cms'
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({ extensions: [cms({ guard: { load: async () => (await import('./src/auth')).auth.guard({ require: 'editor' }) }, files: forgejo({ url, repo: 'me/site', token }) })] })
```

- `cms({ prefix, logo, guard, files, uploads, pageSize, collections, rawHtml, author, onSave })`: `prefix` is where the screens live (`/admin`), `guard` who may use them and the API, as `{ load }` returning the guard, `files` where a folder entry's file goes (`workingTree()` by default, which a production server refuses to boot with unless named). Every option, the upload checks, `rawHtml` and `author` are in [Options of cms()](llms/options.md).
- `forgejo({ url, repo, branch?, token, timeout?, fetch? })`: `url` must be https, or http on `localhost`, `127.x.x.x` or `[::1]`, else it throws, as the token travels in every request; commits each file through Forgejo's contents API, reading the file's current sha first. Throws `ForgeError` with Forgejo's `status` and message, its first 200 characters (the log gets the rest), 504 when the save, its requests together, takes over `timeout` (a duration string, `'15s'`, a bare number throws; the read naming the version after a conflict has its own), or 502 naming why the forge could not be reached; one failing once the commit was sent says it may still have gone through. The editor sees it as the save's issue, the log getting the whole error. Forgejo refusing the commit's sha (409, or 422 naming the sha) throws `SaveConflict`.
- A save or a delete names the version of the file the editor opened, its git blob sha (`fileVersion(text)`): a saver finding the file at another, as after another editor's save, or one's own before the site rebuilt from it, throws `SaveConflict` with the version it found as `current`. The editor keeps the refusal shown while the editor types, and its Keep my edits button takes that version as the one the edits were made from, so the next save writes them over it; nothing else is lost. A new entry must not exist yet. An app's own `FileSaver` checks `change.base` the same way, `null` meaning the file must not exist and `undefined` writing whatever is there; `workingTree()` checks and writes one save of a file at a time.
- The API refuses a save or a delete naming no version for a folder entry the server holds, as from an editor older than the server, logging it: reloading the page loads the editor that names it. A delete from the entry list names the version the list showed, and one from the editor after Keep my edits over a file deleted and made again since names none, so it is refused with a message telling the editor to reload rather than that it is older. Edits kept over a file deleted meanwhile are written as a new entry, refused if the file was made since.
- A loaded entry is versioned the same way with no help from the loader: its version is a hash of the `body` and the `data` fields the schema declares that the loader gave for it (`contentVersion`, key order ignored, so a loader adding or changing undeclared fields causes no conflict), which the editor names on a save or a delete, from the entry list too. A save or delete over an entry that has changed since, by another editor or by the app, is refused with `conflict` carrying the hash it is at now (`null` once deleted, which Keep my edits writes again as new), and a save answers the hash it left for the next one, so one editor saving twice never conflicts, nor does a stale save over a change that left the content as it was. The check reads the entry through the loader before the write, and the check, write and re-read of one collection's saves and deletes run one after the other in the server (not across servers); a loader giving a field that differs on every read conflicts on every save. A versioned save costs two more loader reads, a delete one.
- A file whose blob sha is not what `fileVersion` gives conflicts on every save: a repository checked out with CRLF line endings the server converts, or one using SHA-256 object names.
- Saving again while a save is on its way waits for it, then saves the edits typed meanwhile once.
- `workingTree()`: writes or deletes the file in place, for `kay dev`, or a server whose files outlive a deploy.
- A folder collection's source files ship with the server: kay throws for a folder missing from the build, and for one outside the repository. Slugs follow kay's rules, and a file that does not parse lists as broken, its form opening empty to write over it, a Markdown file keeping its body. A collection whose loader throws is listed as one that cannot be read, its error going to the server's log rather than the screens, which may name a database or its credentials.

## Screens

The screens fit a 375 px phone: no sideways scroll, lists stacked as cards, controls big enough to tap (covered in `tests/fixture/tests/site.test.ts`).

- `<prefix>`: each collection with its entry count.
- `<prefix>/collections/<collection>`: its entries, 50 a page, titled by their first one-line text field, searched, filtered and sorted from the URL, ticked for bulk actions, duplicated ([the list](llms/screens.md#the-list)), with Publish for a draft, Edit on page for an entry kay knows the page of, and Delete. A collection declaring `publishAt: '<date field>'` (see Drafts in kay's content guide) has a Status column marking a published entry whose date is ahead, and the entry screen the same badge beside the form's date field, both in the editor's own zone (`Scheduled for 2026-10-20 10:00 GMT+2`, `UTC` until the browser says it) and gone when the date passes (`Published` in the list), with no reload; an editor sets, changes or clears the field; the cms only edits the field, kay publishes the entry at that time. A collection declaring `order: '<number field>'` lists its entries in that order with Up and Down on each (none while searching); a move writes the field of the two entries swapping places, or numbers the entries of that locale from 1 when their values repeat or are missing, each a save (`save` for a loaded collection), and stops at the first one refused.
- `<prefix>/collections/<collection>/<slug>` (`?locale=`): the entry's form, headed by its title under its crumbs (Content, then its collection), its slug beneath, and Save (disabled until something changed, also on Ctrl or Cmd+S), Reset, Publish or Unpublish, Delete and Edit on page beside it, with where the entry stands (Saving…, Unsaved changes, or Saved at the time, adding that the site shows it once it has rebuilt, with a link to the page, after a commit). The fields are locked while a save is on its way. Publish and Unpublish change the draft flag alone: with unsaved edits they refuse, and a refused save puts the flag back. A scheduled entry has Publish now and Clear schedule beside its badge; a collection declaring `unpublishAt: '<date field>'` shows `Ends <date>` beside the form while that date is ahead and `Ended` once it passes, with Clear end date beside it (the field itself is edited like any date). Delete names the entry and, for one with a page, warns that the page stops answering.
- A collection declaring `single: true` (and optionally `seed: { ... }`, see Collections in kay's content docs) is one entry: the content list links straight to its form, titled with the collection's `title`, with no slug field, New entry or Delete (the way back is the content list), `<prefix>/collections/<collection>` redirects to it, and `saveEntry` refuses a second entry and `deleteEntry` any delete. A new entry's form opens filled with the `seed`; its slug is `index`.
- `<prefix>/new/<collection>` (`?locale=`): a new entry, its slug and in a localized collection its locale, one the site serves. A folder collection's slug is written from the title until it is typed in (a checkbox turns that off), cleaned as typed (Latin accents dropped, other scripts kept with their marks (Greek accents, Arabic vowel signs), spaces and case: `Été à la ferme` is `ete-a-la-ferme`, `/` kept between folders; a title with no letter or digit says to type one), flagged and marked invalid as soon as the collection holds it, and says which folder it lands in, creates, or looks like a typo of (`GET /api/cms/slugs/:collection` lists the slugs). A loaded collection's slug stays as typed.
- `<prefix>/translations`: in a site with two locales or more, per localized collection the entries missing a locale or holding a text still as the default locale's (`title`, `summary` and the body; a field with a `format` or wrapped in `untranslated()` is left out). An entry's screen links its locales (a missing one starts a draft copy of it), `?compare=<locale>` shows another's text beside the form, a text equal to or empty beside the default locale's is said under its field, and the entries list flags the locales an entry lacks.
- `<prefix>/media`: the media library, every upload with its preview, size and the entries using it, renamed or deleted from there.
- `<prefix>/uploads`: the unused uploads, each with its variants and a Delete that asks first; ticked rows are deleted together, the content read once for all.
- `<prefix>/not-found`: the pages visitors asked for and found nothing at, most visited first, as the production server counted them (kay's `data/not-found.sqlite`), with the hosts they came from, the site's own pages that linked there (needs the request's `Host` to match the site's), the time of the last visit, a suggested target; paths a redirect answers are left out. Each row has Dismiss (it is listed again when asked for again; Clear the list and the selection do many), Gone (a 410) and an Add redirect button (a box offering the site's pages holding what is typed, `GET /api/cms/redirects/paths?q=`, when none is suggested), which writes the redirect (a 307, a 308 with its Permanent box ticked) to the file the running server reads (`addRuntimeRedirect` in `kay/library`, same-site targets only, loops and targets no page serves refused) so it answers at once and the path leaves the list, and a table of the redirects added here with Edit (the same path takes a new target or status), Remove and a selection, then the config's, read-only. They call `POST /api/cms/redirects` with `{ from, to, status? }` (307, 308, 410 or a kept 301 or 302, answering 400 with the refusal), `/remove` with `{ froms }`, `/dismiss` with `{ paths }` and `/clear`. Both need the app's `guard` and the same rules as the `redirects` of kay.config.ts: kay's llms/routing-endpoints-and-base.md, Redirects. Copying the `redirects` line into kay.config.ts stays possible.
- `<prefix>/page?path=`: opens the page in edit mode.
- A page of the app at a screen's path replaces it (under `src/routes/(admin)/` for prefix `/`, which keeps the cms's layout and guard), and `<prefix>/_layout.kay` of the app replaces the cms's layout (its own chrome with a nav and a link back to the site, `Toaster`, `TooltipHost`, `@kaynooo/kayjs-cms/admin.css`); the screens set `layouts: false` and `noindex: true`, so the site's header, footer, layout CSS and head tags never reach them, their titles end in `Content admin` (`cms.admin.brand`), and words `cms.admin.skip`, `cms.admin.navigation`, `cms.admin.viewSite` are new; the parts the screens are made of are exported: see [Arranging and replacing the screens](llms/screens.md).

## API

- `fieldsOf(schema)`: the form fields of a collection's JSON Schema, in order, each `{ key, label, required, hint, kind }`. Kinds: `text`, `textarea`, `lines`, `markdown`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `image`, `file`, `json`, `select` (an enum or a union of literals, with `options`, each `{ value, label, raw }`; a literal's `title` is its label), `reference` (with `collection`), `list` (with `item`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, and `blocks` for a `blocks()` list, each `{ type, label, fields }` ([Blocks](llms/fields.md#blocks)); a list of single controls shows one label, then compact rows, a list of groups, lists or files heads each item with its own title (the first filled `text` field of a group, else `Item N` or the item schema's title) that folds it away; each item has up, down, duplicate and remove buttons, and Alt+Shift with an arrow key moves the item in focus (not from a textarea, where macOS selects a paragraph with it); a move is said to screen readers as `Moved {item} to {position} of {count}`, a numbered item named by the place it left; the list shows its item count and `minItems`/`maxItems`, Add and Duplicate stop at the maximum and Remove at the minimum; a new item starts as the item schema's `default`, else blank, a select staying unpicked; removing an item offers Undo, and focus lands on the item that took its place, or on the new item after Add) and `group` (with `fields`), and `custom` (with `name`, a kind the app's `customField` names). kay's `x-kay: { kind }` hint wins over the type. A `datetime` (an `s.Date()` is one) is shown and typed on the wall clock of the editor's browser zone (UTC on the server render and until the browser mounts), with a hint naming it, `Time in Europe/Paris`, and stores the instant it names as a full UTC date, so the entry says the same at any editor's zone; a time the zone's clocks skip is stored an hour on, as a `Date` reads it, and one they repeat at its first turn; clearing a date field stores nothing. A nullable field is optional. `s.Integer()`, `s.Numeric()`, `s.BooleanString()` and `s.Date()`, which accept a string too, are read as their plain kind.
- `fieldOf(key, schema, required)`: the one field a property's JSON Schema makes, as `fieldsOf` makes each, `key` a number for a list item (labelled `Item 1`, `Item 2`).
- `humanize(key)`: a key as words for a label, `publishedAt` as `Published at`, an acronym keeping its capitals, `seoURL` as `Seo URL`, `_` and `-` only separating words, as the screens title a collection with no `title`.
- `emptyValue(field)`: what a new list item starts as.
- `parseMarker(value, body?)`, `formatMarker(marker)`, `entryKey(ref)`: read and write kay's markers.
- `fieldsAt(node)`: the fields rendered at a node, innermost first.
- `createDrafts({ show, delay, keep })`: the unsaved edits of a page's entries; `keep` is a `DraftKeeper` (`browserKeeper()`) holding them across a reload, none by default. `anyChanged()`, `discardAll()`, `recovery(ref)`, `adopt(ref, entry, version)` and `differences(ref, other)` serve the leave guard, Stop editing and the conflict choice. `open(entry, version?)`, `version(ref)`, `value(ref, path)`, `set(ref, path, value)`, `changed(ref)`, `reset(ref)`, `markSaved(ref, sent, version?)` (what was sent becomes the saved state, an edit typed meanwhile staying unsaved), `refuse(ref, refusal)`, `refusal(ref)` and `keepEdits(ref)` (why a save was refused as a whole, kept until the entry saves or resets, and taking a conflict's version), `issues(ref, path?)`, `failure()`, `rendering()`, `stale()` (the changed entries the last render or save reported issues for, whose saved text the page shows) and `reapply()` (renders again with the edits, for a page that replaced the one they were shown on). Each change renders the page with every changed entry once typing pauses `delay` (a duration, `'150ms'`), keeping only the latest render's issues; `report(issues)` shows a refused save's, which a render scheduled before it leaves be until the next edit.
- `valueAt(data, path)`, `withValueAt(data, path, value)`, `joinPath(parent, key)`: field paths.

## Dev tool

- `cms()` adds a CMS tab to the dev tool under `kay dev`, with nothing to add in the app: whether the visitor is in edit mode, a button into it for the page shown (through the screens' `page` route, so the guard decides) and one out of it (the `preview/exit` route). It reads `/_kay/cms`, a route mounted under `kay dev` alone.

## More

- [Options of cms()](llms/options.md): `prefix`, `logo`, `guard`, `files`, `uploads` and their checks, `pageSize`, `collections`, `rawHtml`, `author`, `onSave`
- [Arranging and replacing the screens](llms/screens.md): `cms({ collections })` for a form's field order, rows and hidden fields and a list's columns and row actions; an app's page at a screen's path; `createEntryForm` and the entry parts to build an entry screen
- [Uploads and image fields](llms/uploads.md): what a file or image field does, the upload route and its limits, the picker, alt text and sizes kept beside an image, and the unused-uploads screen
- [History, the trash and the activity log](llms/history.md): the last 50 saves of a loaded entry and its deleted entries for 30 days, restorable, and who did what, kept by default; `cms({ history })` and a loader's `sibling`
- [Loaders and a live CMS](llms/loaders.md): `sqliteLoader` and `postgresLoader`, seeding, all-or-nothing saves of several entries, the steps to wire editors saving on a running site, how other processes and outside edits are followed (`watch`), and `onSave`
- [Edit this page link](llms/page-links.md): the link an editor's browser finds on each page, `pageLink: false`, a link of your own, and how an entry finds its page
- [Field kinds and entering a field](llms/fields.md): `fieldInput` (placeholder, unit, rows, labels, lines, when), what the schema sets, `customField`, `blocks`, ready-made kinds (`colorField`, `moneyField`, `tagsField`, `linkField`, `geoField`, `iconField`)
- [Renaming an entry's slug](llms/rename.md): the Rename button, the old URL redirecting by itself, a saver's `move`
- [Texts and languages](llms/words.md): the `cms.*` messages that word every text of the screens and the editor
